text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a result which has led to a six-fold increase in the number of warrants on issue over the last year, Australia's warrant market has exploded, with monthly turnover increasing almost five-fold to A$140 million over the past 12 months. At the same time, he number of investors holding warrants is now estimated to be more than 30,000. Page 1.

Ansett executive chairman Rod Eddington has indicated he is set to follow the lead of rival Qantas and take a hard line on operational costs as part of a strategy to rebuild Ansett's earnings base, which is hoped will provide a sound base for when the comany is floated. Page 23.

Mercantile Mutual Holdings managing director Rod Atfield said the company's funds management and life insurance were the driving forces behind the its 70 per cent rise in net profit to A$54.6 million in the six months to March 31, which is a substantial mprovement to last year's comparable figure of A$32.1. Page 23.

South Australian Mines and Energy Minister Stephen Baker has announced the go-ahead for a A$1 billion iron ore project after the discovery of a eight iron-ore deposits totalling 850 million tonnes of magnetite and hermatite in an area 120 kilometres southof Cooper Pedy. Page 26.

Mining giant WMC yesterday released its environmental impact statement into the A$3 billion Olympic Dam copper/uranium mine, which it hopes will pave the way for approval from State and Federal Governments for the company to treat 17 million tonnes of ore a year and process 350,000 tonnes of copper cathode. Page 27.

HIH Winterthur chief executive Ray Williams has told the company's annual general meeting that the general insurer is well on target to smash the A$1 billion net premium income barrier this year, saying that the acquisition of US company HealthCal and Colnial Mutual's general insurance operations last year has significantly helped the insurer. Page 29.
THE AUSTRALIAN

National Australia Bank Ltd's interim profit is expected to be over A$1 billion for the first time when figures for the six months to March 31 are released this week. While ANZ and Westpac's figures are forecast to be around A$600 million, NAB is expecting an interim profit of A$1.17 billion, a rise from A$995 million. Page 29.

Details about the content of the upcoming Federal Budget remain unknown outside of the ministerial wing of Parliament, although it is known the number of expenditure or saving intiatives for the coming year are relatively small as the key economic thrust is the challenge to bring the Budget deficit to balance. Page 29.

Key findings from the National Australian Bank's monthly business survey indicate business confidence is still under pressure, with a pickup in activity across sectors yet to eventuate. Annual growth is stuck between 2.5 and three per cent, compared withthe 1996-97 Budget forecast of 3.5 per cent, and 1997-98 predictions of four per cent. Page 29.

Mining company WMC Ltd is planning a fivefold increase in uranium production at its Olympic Dam mine at South Australia's Roxby Downs by 2010. WMC also proposes to lift annual copper production from 85,000 to 200,000 tonnes by 200 and uranium oxide prodution from 1500 to 4630 tonnes. Page 31.

Insurance and financial services group Mercantile Mutual Holdings Ltd has failed to secure control of the NSW-based Axiom superannuation group. Mercantile retains its bid of A$100 million, and is expected to post a record full-year profit after an interi net profit of A$54.6 million for the six months to March 31. Page 31.

Wesfarmers Dalgety Wool Supply Outlook has forecasted wool production will record its first increase for seven years after the release of a national survey of wool growers. The expected rise of three percent in production and a two per cent increase in seep numbers should occur due to better seasonal conditions and a slowdown in the shift to cropping and away from wool production. Page 31.

THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD Australia's biggest bank, the National Australia Bank, is expected to again be the industry's most profitable bank, with predictions it will post the biggest increase in half-year earnings. Analysts are confident lost income from the mortgage war will beoffset by rising volumes, substantial efficiency improvements and a pay-off from earlier technology investments. Page 37.

Institutional investors are expected to bid up to A$3.10 per share for a stake in Colonial as a limited number of stock is offered this week. Colonial will be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange on May 19 of this year, and the company will seek instiutional stability in its stock-holders. Page 37.

Telstra is expecting to compete head-first with banks in the clearing and settling of transactions if there is to be a Wallis-inspired liberalisation of the financial system. The company wishes to be at the forefront of smart card and Internet transactio technology, but will not offer products of its own. Page 37.

Comments yesterday by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello are destroying hopes the Federal Government would announce an underlying surplus in Tuesday's Budget and have joined the three per cent drop in value of Australian and US dollars against the yen in creating anxiety within financial markets. Page 39.

In a bold attempt to cut programming costs and force an industry-wide restructuring, pay-TV group Australis Media is considering replacing the Discovery, Arena, Nickelodeon and V music channels, supplied by XYZ Entertainment, with cheaper options. The chnge would replace these channels with others bought directly from offshore. Page 39.

ICI Australia managing director Warren Haynes said yesterday he expected foreign ownership of the company would amount to 50 per cent of the 62.4 per cent stake on the market if a contender like American chemicals company Dow did not buy 100 per cent of he company when its British parents offloads its stake in July. Page 39.
THE AGE

AMP has remained coy on a UK newspaper report that the Australian insurance group intends to launch a take-over bid for Norwich Union, which is on the verge of a A$10 billion London Stock Exchange listing. The speculation comes only two months after AMP as defeated by rival Prudential in the take-over bid for Scottish Amicable. Page B1.

Eager to become a player in the smart-card and Internet transaction market, Telstra has announced it intends competing with the banks in the clearing and settling of transactions if there is a liberalisation of the financial market in the wake of the Walls Report. Telstra will announce today the details of a $A100 million investment plan to replace its phone cards with smart cards. Page B1.

Investors in the fake Bre-X minerals mine have signalled they intend to take a class action lawsuit against a major brokerage firm involved in the deal, as Canadian authorities announce they have assigned 10 officers from the Royal Canadian Mounted Policeto form a special fraud squad to investigate the scandal. Page B1.

PBL chairman James Packer said yesterday he is opposed to any proposed legislation which would limit a merged PBL-Fairfax group from owning one newspaper and a TV station in the one city - a move which would effectively force the sell off the Australian Financial Review. Page B1.

The sharemarket has expressed optimism ahead of tomorrow night's Federal Budget with predictions of positive results in today's housing finance figures, which are expected to confirm an upswing in the building sector. However, some analysts have warned te Australian dollar could suffer from a plunge in the value of the greenback after a speech last week by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. Page B1.

The Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation Forum has finished its three day meeting in Montreal after agreeing to work towards free trade in financial services and expanding open markets for information technology. Last year's talks on financial services fell thrugh after the United States pulled out after its disappointment in offers from some other countries. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
